decision.trend: Research on refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) has been focused on understanding their mechanical properties at elevated temperatures. Earlier studies have shown that RHEAs exhibit high yield strengths and substantial softening resistance at high temperatures. Recent studies have investigated the effects of composition, microstructure, and deformation mechanisms on the mechanical properties of RHEAs. The trend suggests that controlling the type of mobile dislocations, such as edge dislocations, can improve the strength of RHEAs at high temperatures.
decision.unsolved: The stress-strain behavior, thermal expansion, and elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr RHEA at elevated temperatures remain insufficiently understood. The effects of composition, microstructure, and deformation mechanisms on these properties need to be further investigated.
decision.why: To investigate the elastic and plastic deformation behaviors of HfNbTaTiZr RHEA at elevated temperatures, in situ neutron diffraction can be used to study the temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation behavior and edge dislocation-dominated plastic deformation behaviors. This will provide valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms controlling the mechanical properties of RHEAs at high temperatures.
